s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive visual impairment with endocrinological disturbances and a sellar/suprasellar mass
salient_findings: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
key_facts: 2-week history of rapidly progressive visual reduction
Vestibular schwannoma treated by gamma-knife radiosurgery 2 years earlier
Mass compressing the optic chiasm and extending toward the left cavernous sinus
Lesion predominantly isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images
Diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration
Normal pituitary gland on previous MRI

shortlist.label: Pituitary macroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm, elevated prolactin level, and abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone level

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass, isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images, and history of vestibular schwannoma

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive visual impairment, endocrinological disturbances, and sellar/suprasellar mass

shortlist.label: Pituitary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass, abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone level, and elevated prolactin level

raw.rationale: The patient's rapidly progressive visual reduction, bitemporal hemianopsia, and sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm are consistent with a pituitary macroadenoma. The MRI characteristics, including a mass that is isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images with diffuse homogeneous enhancement, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Typically presents with calcifications on imaging, which were not mentioned

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Usually has a dural tail on imaging and is less likely to cause rapid visual decline

rejected.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with symptoms of hypopituitarism and has a more inflammatory appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Pituitary carcinoma
rejected.why: Is a rare and aggressive tumor, and the patient's presentation is more consistent with a benign macroadenoma
